column1: # Game profile of Stardew Valley (Switch, update 1.6.15.13 = v1310720; base game v0 not extracted). Plays on the Mac (title, a new farm, the farm, the bus stop and Pelican Town, the menus, a night's sleep and its save, at 60 fps with sound) and on the iPhone
# MonoGame for the Switch (Microsoft.Xna.Framework over NVN), its C# compiled to C++ into main (124 MB of code), XACT sound (Content/XACT) through the audio renderer, SDK 20.5.27.

# The shaders are MonoGame effects (MGFX version 8): SpriteBatch's and the game's own in main, and Content/Effects/ShadowRemove.xnb, an LZ4-compressed XNB (shader_split.py mgfx_effect, xnb_decompress). Nearly everything draws with SpriteBatch.
# Input is the pad only (main imports no touch screen or mouse): the D-pad moves between menu items, the right stick the cursor, ZL / ZR the toolbar slot. The provisional profile's guesses held

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# only the merged 1.6.15.13 copy is extracted
# The NPDM declares no system resource, so the game has no virtual address memory: it sets a heap of the application pool − used memory (2.96 GB) and allocates from it.
# The block is 256 MB in front + 256 MB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 3.25 GB heap region
# the NPDM declares no system resource: IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is false, as on Horizon

# the rewritten modules are larger than the default 64 MB of used memory (214 MB without main's 29.6 MB of bss, + 4 MB: dm/games/profile_guess.py mem_used), so the heap request plus the modules would exceed the pool
# the 3D layout: the D-pad for menus and the right stick for the cursor
